Looping you in on Nimbus questions. They want explicit language on physical tenancy and an automated failover/fencing flow. Laura — legal will need the wording around "reserved pools will not host other tenants"; Priyom/Neha — ops/eng, can we confirm what our exact failover behavior is when a fenced pool reports NodeFailed?

Summary of what I expect we can offer:
- Reserved pools are logically dedicated; on our managed Hosted offering we guarantee node-level isolation via pool assignment. For Private deployments we can provide customer-managed VPCs and dedicated nodes.
- Fencing: unhealthy nodes are evicted from the reserved pool; requests are automatically routed to a warm standby pool of compatible model variants; if warm standby is exhausted, requests fall back to a broader shared tier with documented SLA degradation.

We need a clear ops checklist and an example paragraph for the SOW. I'll get a first pass and send to legal.

Rishi / team —

Confirmed behavior from infra:

- Reserved pools are bound at allocation time to customer IDs; allocation includes node labels and taints to avoid scheduling other tenants. In Hosted this is enforced by our scheduler and runtime. For Dedicated, we provision exclusive nodes in the pool.
- On NodeFailed we quarantine the node (mark NotReady), evict KV caches, and rotate the node out of the routing ring. Requests are diverted to the warm standby pool; standby capacity is pre-reserved as part of the commitment (we usually suggest 10% of committed GPUs).
- We can add a contractual paragraph stating "Redwood will not schedule third-party tenant workloads on the reserved pool allocated to Nimbus during the term of the agreement."

I've attached a short ops checklist (tenant-separation-ops-checklist.csv) that the on-call can run during the cutover.

If legal wants specific notification windows for node replacement or planned maintenance, we'll propose 48 hours notice for non-emergency maintenance and 4 hours for emergency remediation.

—Priyom
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

   "Redwood will not schedule third-party tenant workloads on the reserved pool allocated to Customer during the term of the agreement."
